name: Account for leases and expected credit losses (equipment finance company)
summary: Each month the lessor must show its leases at the right value: finance leases as receivables earning income at a constant rate, operating leases as depreciating assets, residual values that still hold, and an allowance for the credit losses it expects. Lease accountants check the classification of new contracts, review finance income, modifications and residual values, while portfolio risk analysts run the IFRS 9 expected credit loss model on month-end data with forward-looking scenarios; the accounting manager and controller review the results, a quarterly committee approves scenarios and adjustments, and the entries go to the month-end close. The work is slow and error-prone because the model and most reviews live in spreadsheets fed from the data warehouse, classification and residual judgements need experience, and 2020 payment deferrals and swings in the economic outlook made the allowance hard to estimate.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian equipment lessor with 55,000 active contracts and $1.5 billion of net investment reporting under IFRS, with audited statements relied on by its bank syndicate and conduits.
baseline.notes: IFRS 16 applied from 1 January 2019 (lessor accounting largely unchanged from IAS 17) and IFRS 9 from 2018; a lease management system with month-end batch, a data warehouse, and spreadsheet models for classification review, residuals and expected credit losses.

trigger: The month-end cut-off in the lease system, with the month's booked contracts, the monthly risk report and the latest residual schedule available.
end_state: Classification, income, modification and residual entries and the expected credit loss allowance are approved, posted and reconciled to the ledger and handed to the month-end close, with quarter-end disclosure schedules when due.

volume.seasonality: Quarter ends add scenario updates, the committee review and disclosure schedules; year end adds the audit. 2020 brought thousands of payment deferrals and large swings in forward-looking scenarios.

evidence.note: One cycle a month, as in the organisation file's process map.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Document imaging and contract file store

steps.name: Lease system runs the month-end batch
steps.description: After the month-end cut-off the lease system closes the period overnight: it accrues finance income on every finance lease and loan, depreciates operating lease assets, amortises initial direct costs, ages receivables and loads a month-end contract snapshot to the data warehouse.

error.defect_description: A batch job fails or loads a partial snapshot.

evidence.note: Finance income at a constant periodic rate and operating lease depreciation are required by IFRS 16; the overnight batch matches the close-the-month workflow (step s02).

steps.name: Extract the month's new bookings and classification report
steps.description: A lease accountant runs the report of contracts booked in the month (about 1,400) with lease type code, term, equipment type, purchase option, residual, implicit rate and cost, and filters the ones the classification rules flag: fair market value or large fixed residuals, terms short against the equipment's life, mid-ticket deals and new product codes.

error.defect_description: A filter misses a new product code.

evidence.note: Flag rules are an author estimate; most small-ticket leases with nominal purchase options are finance leases (book-contracts workflow assumption).

steps.name: Review the classification of flagged contracts
steps.description: For each flagged contract the accountant opens the schedule in the imaging system, checks the purchase option, term against economic life, residual and present value of payments against the equipment cost, and decides whether the lease transfers substantially all the risks and rewards; they record the conclusion in the review workbook.

error.defect_description: A fair market value lease with a large residual left as a finance lease.

control.basis: IFRS 16 paragraphs 61 to 66: lease classification at inception by transfer of risks and rewards

next.condition: one or more lease type codes wrong

evidence.note: Classification criteria from the standard; about 100 to 150 flagged contracts a month at 3 to 5 minutes each is an author estimate.

steps.name: Correct lease type codes and prepare the reclassification
steps.description: The accountant sends the booking team the contracts whose accounting class is wrong, with the correct code, and drafts the journal that moves them between net investment in finance leases and operating lease assets, including the depreciation or income already recorded.

error.defect_description: The correction is made in the ledger but not in the lease system, so the difference recurs.

evidence.note: Classification is set at inception and not reassessed for estimate changes, so a wrong code is an error to correct; waiting for the booking team is an author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile new bookings and initial direct costs
steps.description: The accountant ties the net investment added in the month to the vendor payments and broker commissions funded and to the booking journal from the lease system, and checks that broker fees and other initial direct costs are deferred on the right contracts.

error.defect_description: A commission booked as an expense instead of deferred.

evidence.note: Initial direct costs are included in the net investment for lessors that are not dealers or manufacturers; minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Review finance income and amortisation for anomalies
steps.description: The accountant compares the month's finance income yield by product and channel with prior months and with the booked rates, and lists contracts with zero, negative or very high yields, usually from a wrong rate, a missed payment change or a modification booked incorrectly.

error.defect_description: A systematic rate error is accepted as normal.

evidence.note: Finance income must give a constant periodic rate of return; the analytical review and the 20% rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Investigate and correct income anomalies
steps.description: For each anomaly the accountant reads the contract and its transaction history, works out the correct income, and either asks operations to fix the schedule or prepares a correcting entry for the difference.

error.defect_description: A correction posted in the wrong period.

evidence.note: Typical follow-up of an income review; minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Account for modifications, deferrals and terminations
steps.description: The accountant works the month's report of restructures, payment deferrals, assumptions, early buyouts and casualty terminations, checks that each was remeasured correctly in the lease system, records any modification loss on finance leases and treats changed operating leases as new leases.

error.defect_description: A deferral remeasured without the loss on the delayed payments.

control.basis: IFRS 16 paragraph 66 and IFRS 9: modified leases reassessed and remeasured

evidence.note: Modifications trigger reassessment and a delay in payment creates a credit loss; the high end reflects the 2020 deferral wave the organisation file describes; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Review residual values against the residual schedule
steps.description: The accountant compares the unguaranteed residuals booked on fair market value and fixed-option contracts with the latest residual schedule from asset management and recent remarketing results, by equipment type and maturity year, and lists types where the expected residual has fallen.

error.defect_description: A fall in residuals on one equipment type is missed.

control.basis: IFRS 16 paragraph 77: lessor shall review regularly estimated unguaranteed residual values

next.condition: reductions indicated for some equipment types

evidence.note: The review is required by the standard; monthly frequency and the 40% rate of flagged types are author estimates.

steps.name: Asset manager confirms revised residual estimates
steps.description: An asset manager reviews the flagged equipment types against auction results, dealer listings and recent off-lease sales and confirms or adjusts the expected residuals, with a short note of the evidence.

error.defect_description: An optimistic residual retained on thin evidence.

evidence.note: Asset managers maintain residual tables (organisation file process value-equipment-and-set-residuals); queue time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Calculate and record the residual impairment
steps.description: The accountant revises the income allocation for the affected finance leases and calculates the immediate charge for amounts already accrued, and for operating lease assets adjusts depreciation or tests for impairment, preparing the journal and support.

error.defect_description: Charge calculated on the wrong population of contracts.

evidence.note: Paragraph 77 requires revising the income allocation and recognising the reduction immediately; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Extract the month-end credit loss data
steps.description: A portfolio risk analyst extracts contract-level balances, days past due, risk grade or score band, deferral and restructure flags, watch list, insolvency status and equipment type from the data warehouse and the monthly risk report, and ties the total exposure to the lease subledger.

error.defect_description: Sold conduit contracts or new bookings missing from the extract.

evidence.note: Exposure, default probability and loss inputs come from risk data and risk management is involved in measuring allowances; the step runs in parallel with the lease accountant's work in practice.

steps.name: Assign stages and run the expected credit loss model
steps.description: The analyst assigns each contract a stage (stage 2 for a significant increase in credit risk, such as 30 days past due, a deferral or watch list; stage 3 for 90 days past due, default or insolvency) and runs the spreadsheet model that applies default probabilities by score band or risk rating, loss given default by equipment type and the exposure at default.

error.defect_description: Stage rules applied to the wrong field or a stale parameter table used.

control.basis: IFRS 9 section 5.5: impairment measured as expected credit losses, lifetime for credit-impaired and significantly deteriorated exposures

next.condition: quarter end or a change in the economic outlook
parameters and scenarios unchanged this month

evidence.note: Three-stage approach with default probability, loss given default and exposure at default as a Canadian equipment lender describes it; this lessor is assumed to use the general approach for lease receivables, which is a policy choice.

steps.name: Update forward-looking scenarios and weights
steps.description: The analyst updates the base, upside and downside economic scenarios from the large Canadian banks' published forecasts (unemployment, GDP, business insolvencies, used equipment prices), sets the scenario weights, recalculates the adjustments to default probabilities and documents the rationale for any judgement not captured by the model.

error.defect_description: Scenario weights or an overlay set without support.

evidence.note: Base case updated quarterly with other probability-weighted scenarios, forecasts averaged from the large Canadian banks and expert credit judgment for effects such as government support that models cannot capture; the high end reflects 2020.

steps.name: Analyse the allowance movement and draft commentary
steps.description: The analyst builds the allowance roll-forward (opening balance, new bookings, stage transfers, write-offs, recoveries, remeasurement and scenario changes), compares coverage by stage with last month and with net charge-offs, and writes the commentary for accounting.

error.defect_description: A movement explained by the wrong driver.

evidence.note: Allowance reconciliation by stage with remeasurement from macroeconomic forecasts and qualitative adjustments; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Assess large credit-impaired accounts individually
steps.description: For mid-ticket accounts in default, repossession or insolvency the analyst asks late-stage collections and recoveries for the expected recovery (equipment value after costs, guarantor prospects, trustee estimates) and replaces the modelled amount with an individual allowance where it differs.

error.defect_description: A recovery estimate taken from an out-of-date collection note.

evidence.note: Typical treatment of large impaired exposures; the wait for collections and recoveries input is an author estimate.

steps.name: Accounting manager reviews the lease accounting and allowance package
steps.description: The accounting manager checks the classification conclusions, modification and residual entries, ties the credit loss data to the subledger, reviews the model run, stage movements and commentary, and sends points back to the analyst or accountant.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Internal control over the allowance and lease accounting tested by the external auditor: independent review of a key estimate

next.condition: data or model issue: rerun the model
movement analysis or commentary to rework

evidence.note: Review layer typical of a private lessor whose lenders rely on audited statements; the 20% return rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Controller approves the allowance and management adjustments
steps.description: The controller reviews the allowance level against charge-off experience, delinquency and coverage by stage, challenges any management adjustment and the residual and modification charges, and approves the figures for posting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Allowance for credit losses approved by the controller as a key accounting estimate relied on by auditors and lenders

next.condition: quarter end: credit loss committee review

evidence.note: Typical approval path; the quarter-end share is one in three months.

steps.name: Quarterly credit loss committee approves scenarios and adjustments
steps.description: At quarter end the chief financial officer chairs a meeting with the controller, the chief credit officer and the director of risk and portfolio management that reviews the scenarios, weights, management adjustments and coverage, and approves the allowance for the quarterly statements and lender reporting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Credit loss allowance governance: quarterly senior management approval of scenarios and adjustments

evidence.note: Governance with risk management involvement and expert credit judgment described in supervisory guidance and a lender's report; the committee is an author estimate for a private lessor. Touch time is the chair's.

steps.name: Prepare and post the lease accounting and allowance entries
steps.description: The lease accountant prepares the journal for the change in the allowance by stage, individual allowances, residual impairment, modification losses and reclassifications, attaches the support and uploads it to the ledger.

error.defect_description: Allowance change posted to the wrong stage account or cost centre.

evidence.note: Matches the close-the-month workflow, which ties these entries in at step s10; minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Accounting manager approves the journal in the ledger
steps.description: The accounting manager checks the journal against the approved figures and support and approves it in the ledger; the preparer cannot approve their own entry.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Manual journal entries approved by someone other than the preparer (company journal entry policy)

evidence.note: Same control as the close-the-month workflow (step s12).

steps.name: Reconcile lease and allowance balances to the ledger
steps.description: The accountant ties the net investment, operating lease assets, residuals and the allowance by stage in the ledger to the subledger and the approved roll-forward, files the package for the close and the auditors and notes open items for next month.

error.defect_description: A reconciling item carried without explanation.

evidence.note: Hand-off to close-the-month, whose lease accountant ties the allowance roll-forward to write-offs and recoveries (step s10).

steps.name: Prepare quarter-end lease and credit risk schedules
steps.description: At quarter end the accountant prepares the schedules lenders, the board and the auditors need: the five-year maturity analysis of lease payments receivable, finance income and selling profit, operating lease income, the allowance by stage and the credit quality tables.

error.defect_description: Maturity analysis does not reconcile to the net investment.

control.basis: IFRS 16 paragraphs 89 to 97 and IFRS 7 credit risk disclosures

evidence.note: Paragraph 94 requires a maturity analysis for at least each of the first five years and a reconciliation to the net investment; minutes are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Wrong lease classification code
exceptions.description: Review finds contracts booked with the wrong accounting class, usually fair market value leases set up as finance leases; booking corrects the code and accounting posts a reclassification.

exceptions.name: Income anomalies
exceptions.description: Contracts with zero, negative or very high yields from rate or modification errors are investigated and corrected.

exceptions.name: Residual values fall
exceptions.description: Used equipment values for some types fall below booked residuals; the asset manager confirms revised estimates and accounting records the charge.

exceptions.name: Scenario update
exceptions.description: At quarter end, or when the outlook changes as in March 2020, the analyst updates the scenarios, weights and any management adjustment.

exceptions.name: Package returned on review
exceptions.description: The accounting manager finds a data or model problem or weak commentary and sends the package back for a rerun.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end committee and schedules
exceptions.description: At quarter end the credit loss committee approves the allowance and accounting prepares the lease and credit risk disclosure schedules.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month-end cut-off to approved lease and allowance entries posted
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a private Canadian lessor whose close takes about 11 calendar days

evidence.note: Derived, not observed: the entries must be ready for the controller's review of the draft statements, about business day 5 or 6 of an 11-day close (close-the-month workflow benchmark), and APQC's median close is 6.4 calendar days.

benchmarks.population: 2,300 organisations in APQC's general accounting benchmark
Chesswood Group, $1.7 billion of equipment and vehicle finance receivables

evidence.note: 2020 figure derived from the stated 2021 provision of $0.2 million and the $25.5 million decrease.

benchmarks.population: Canadian Western Bank, including its equipment financing book

pain_points.description: The expected credit loss model is a spreadsheet fed by data warehouse extracts, so each month's run depends on manual data preparation and one or two people who understand it; review often sends it back for a rerun.

evidence.note: Typical of a mid-size non-bank lender without a dedicated model platform; author estimate.

pain_points.description: 2020 payment deferrals and the changing economic outlook forced repeated scenario updates and management adjustments that models could not capture, and the allowance swung sharply between 2020 and 2021.

evidence.note: Chesswood's provision fell from about $25.7 million to $0.2 million; CWB's stage 2 share fell from 34% to 9%.

pain_points.description: Classification and residual reviews need judgement about purchase options, economic lives and used equipment values, and errors in booking codes surface only at month end.

evidence.note: Classification requires considerable professional judgement.

pain_points.description: Modifications from restructures, deferrals and early buyouts are booked by operations and must be rechecked by accounting, because a wrong remeasurement changes income and the allowance.

evidence.note: Author estimate based on the organisation file's restructure and buyout volumes.

sources.title: AASB 16 Leases: lessor requirements (paragraphs 61 to 97), identical in wording to IFRS 16
sources.supports: A lease is a finance lease if it transfers substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership (para 62), with indicators in para 63; classification is made at inception and reassessed only on a modification (para 66); finance income at a constant periodic rate on the net investment (para 75); a lessor shall review regularly estimated unguaranteed residual values and recognise any reduction immediately, and applies IFRS 9 derecognition and impairment to the net investment (para 77); operating lease income and depreciation (paras 81 to 84); disclosures including a five-year maturity analysis (para 94).

sources.title: IFRS 16 (accounting news, October 2018)
sources.supports: Lessor accounting under IFRS 16 is largely unchanged from IAS 17; classification requires considerable professional judgement; a finance lease is a receivable at the net investment with finance income at a constant periodic rate; IFRS 9 impairment applies to finance lease receivables; changes in residual estimates do not change the classification.

sources.title: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments
sources.supports: IFRS 9 is effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2018; the expected credit loss impairment requirements were added in July 2014.

sources.title: Accounting for impairment of lease receivables under IFRS 9
sources.supports: For lease receivables an entity chooses, as an accounting policy, either the general three-bucket approach or the simplified approach that always measures lifetime expected credit losses without tracking changes in credit risk, and must apply the choice consistently.

sources.title: CWB Financial Group Annual Report 2021, significant accounting policies: impairment
sources.supports: Expected credit losses in three stages based on the change in credit risk since initial recognition, measured with probability of default, loss given default and exposure at default; the base case forecast is updated quarterly with a range of other scenarios and multiple probability-weighted outcomes; assessing significant increases in credit risk requires significant judgment.

sources.title: CWB Financial Group Annual Report 2021, MD&A: provision and allowance for credit losses
sources.supports: The macroeconomic forecast is based on an average of the large Canadian banks' forecasts; modelled expected credit losses are supplemented with expert credit judgments, including the effect of government stimulus that cannot be modelled from history; stage 2 loans fell to 9% of performing loans from 34% a year earlier; the performing allowance fell 18% in 2021.

sources.title: CWB Financial Group Annual Report 2021, note on allowance for credit losses by stage
sources.supports: The allowance reconciliation by stage shows transfers, write-offs, recoveries and remeasurement that reflects changes in forward-looking macroeconomic forecasts and qualitative adjustments.

sources.title: Coronavirus impacts on the accounting for financial instruments
sources.supports: COVID-19 may cause a significant increase in credit risk, but deferrals alone should not be assumed to do so across the board; a delay in payment creates a credit loss even when full repayment is expected; expected credit losses are probability-weighted and prior models cannot simply be rolled forward, so entities rework models or apply latest macroeconomic data as an overlay.

sources.title: Guidance on credit risk and accounting for expected credit losses
sources.supports: Supervisory expectations for expected credit loss accounting: risk management should be involved in assessing and measuring allowances; credit loss recognition was too little, too late before the crisis.

sources.title: Chesswood announces fiscal year 2021 results
sources.supports: A North American equipment and vehicle finance group with $1.7 billion of gross finance receivables recognised a $0.2 million provision for credit losses in 2021, $25.5 million less than 2020, mainly from provision releases; net charge-offs were $2.0 million in 2021 against $31.4 million in 2020.

sources.title: Metric of the month: cycle time for monthly close
sources.supports: APQC benchmark of 2,300 organisations: monthly close from trial balance to consolidated statements takes 4.8 calendar days or less for the top quarter, 6.4 days at the median and 10 or more for the bottom quarter.

sources.title: New data reveals market insights (2021 Survey of Equipment Finance Activity)
sources.supports: US equipment finance in 2020: receivables over 30 days past due rose 30 basis points to 2.3%; net full-year losses rose to 0.48% of average receivables.

sources.title: Wages for financial auditors and accountants (NOC 11100)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages for accountants: low $24.73, median $40.87, high $72.12 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: One case is one monthly cycle from the month-end cut-off. Lease accountants and portfolio analysts work in parallel; the simulator adds all hands-on time in sequence, which roughly offsets the fact that about 70 hands-on hours spread over several people's working days; the simulated median of about 9 days sits close to the 8-day estimate.
Lessor accounting is IFRS 16, which carried over IAS 17's lessor model; IFRS 16 text is cited from the Australian standard AASB 16, which reproduces it word for word.

The lessor is assumed to apply the IFRS 9 general three-stage approach to lease and loan receivables, as lenders commonly do; the simplified lifetime approach is an allowed policy choice for lease receivables and would remove stage tracking.

Stage rules (30 days past due, deferrals and watch list for stage 2; 90 days past due, default or insolvency for stage 3) and the use of the large banks' published forecasts follow common Canadian lender practice; this lessor's model is not public.

Portfolio risk analysts own the credit loss data and model because the process map lists them and they produce the monthly risk report; the asset manager (residuals) and chief financial officer (quarterly committee) take part although the process map does not list them.

About 1,400 new bookings a month are classified by a lease type code at booking; only about 100 to 150 flagged contracts are reviewed in detail. Modification volumes are much higher in 2020, which sets the high end of step s08.
Securitised contracts stay on the balance sheet (organisation file assumption), so they remain in the net investment and the allowance.

Staffing: modelled hands-on time is about 70 hours a month, about 0.6 FTE at 130 hours; stated FTE (about 1.3) also covers booking support, audit requests, ad hoc analysis and month-end questions that are not modelled as steps.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
